# ci-state-git

**Read and write CI state in a git repo, committing each record.**

A forge-ci `state` engine.

## Why it exists

Git gives history, atomic writes, auth you already have and an audit trail, for
nothing. It is a normal repo. Read it with `git log`.

## Tools

| Tool | Does |
|---|---|
| `declare` | Report the directories the state repo needs. |
| `get` | Read one record. |
| `put` | Write one record and commit it. |
| `list` | List the keys under one kind. |

## By hand

```sh
echo '{"kind":"revision","key":"abc123","spec":{"path":"../my-state"}}' \
  | ci-state-git get
```

## In a pipeline

```yaml
engines:
  - alias: my-state
    type: state
    engine: "forge://github.com/alexandremahdhaoui/forge-ci/cmd/ci-state-git@v0.1.4"
    manager: local
    spec:
      path: <string>
      kinds: <list of string>
```

## Worth knowing

Kinds are `revision`, `run` and `owned`, plus any extras named in `spec.kinds`.
A run key nests as `<revision>/<stage>/<substage>`, and `list` walks nested keys
recursively.

A key cannot escape the state root. `../../escape` lands inside it.

A missing record is `found: false`, never an error. Nothing to commit is not an
error either.
